newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers on dollar sales, seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers on dollar sales, seen rangebound.

text.p: * Ringgit recovered on fresh dollar sales by offshore and local players
* Further short-covering helped the dollar earlier
The ringgit recovered in early Asian trading on fresh selling of the dollar by local and offshore players, dealers said.

"There was further short-covering from yesterday at the opening but the (dollar) rise was capped at 2.5160. Sellers are out again and we should see a tight range trading today," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur.

Dealers said the dollar might test higher levels against the ringgit but Bank Negara's recent firm stance on speculative activities and fears of central bank intervention should cap its rise at 2.5200.
Players sold the dollar/ringgit on Wednesday amid talk that Bank Negara had warned local banks about lending money offshore to speculative funds.
The talk gave the ringgit some relief against the dollar as ringgit sentiment had been affected by a huge Malaysian trade deficit in April.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5148/58 a dollar against 2.5142/52 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
Dealers said they expected dollar/ringgit to trade in a 2.4950-2.5200 range in the near-term.
